statements.quote: We have hope on the horizon. Psychedelic medicines like LSD have promising early clinical data and more coming in GAD (pre-print from my group).
statements.context: Closing section of a post on benzodiazepines and suicide risk. The author says better anxiety treatments are needed and expects more clinical data on LSD for generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), citing a pre-print from his own research group.
statements.note: Vague; expects more LSD-in-GAD clinical data. Author's own group (control candidate).

statements.quote: These treatments should move into acute care settings. SAINT fMRI guided accelerated neuromodulation in acute care settings needs broader deployment and payment models beyond Medicare.
statements.context: Same closing section. After naming psychedelics and FDA-cleared neuromodulation for anxious depression, the author says these treatments should move into acute care settings and that SAINT accelerated TMS needs broader deployment and payment models beyond Medicare.
statements.note: Normative advice with no explicit prediction; logged for recall.

statements.quote: It was such a hit…there will be more of these real-life newsletter events coming.
statements.context: Recap of RAMHT 2024, the newsletter's first in-person event, held in San Francisco before JPM and co-founded with Grady Hannah. The author says more real-life newsletter events will follow.
statements.note: Author's own newsletter and event series (control candidate).

statements.quote: We are also dedicating a subsection of The Frontier Psychiatrists to ongoing coverage of rapid-acting mental health treatments. It will be up there in the top bar under “RAMHT.”
statements.context: Same recap. The newsletter will add a RAMHT subsection in its top navigation bar for ongoing coverage of rapid-acting mental health treatments.
statements.note: Author's own newsletter (control candidate); format change.

statements.quote: if it's not paid for under a rubric that the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services understands, then it's not gonna be available to the vast majority of people covered by Medicare. Then, most commercial insurance follows Medicare's lead.
statements.context: RAMHT 2024 takeaway attributed to Carlene MacMillan, M.D. (Fermata; Clinical TMS Society board), introduced with 'points out'. Claim: novel rapid-acting treatments will not reach most Medicare patients unless CMS pays for them under a rubric it understands, and commercial insurers follow Medicare.
entities: Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services
statements.note: Quoted third party (Carlene MacMillan, author's spouse and Fermata colleague); author endorses via 'points out'. Conditional, general.

statements.quote: Only rarely performing procedures like obtaining IV access? This means, reliably , it will get messed up—because some individuals’ veins are difficult to access.
statements.context: Post on Alabama's nitrogen-gas execution of Kenneth Eugene Smith after a failed lethal injection in 2022. The author argues that because physicians may not participate in executions, IV access by amateurs will reliably fail in some future executions.
statements.note: General prediction about future lethal injections; compound with the 'reliably unreliable' statement from the same post.

statements.quote: given the prohibition by the AMA ... it will reliably go badly enough of the time to make this “reliably unreliable”—and I am arguing that this means it’s cruel and unusual punishment.
statements.context: Same post. The author predicts lethal injection will reliably go badly often enough to be 'reliably unreliable' because the AMA bars physicians from assisting in executions, and argues this makes it cruel and unusual punishment.
statements.note: Ellipsis skips inline footnote markers. Restates the IV-access prediction; the second half is a legal argument, not a forecast.

statements.quote: And so I am willing to try, knowing I will fail.
statements.context: Personal essay after a rejection from the 2023 Florida Review Editor's Prize; the author entered 36 poetry contests. He expects to keep submitting poetry and to keep losing.
statements.note: Personal, self-referential statement about future poetry submissions; low stakes; logged for recall.

statements.quote: Pre-prints may be a bit of a jailbreak? We shall see.
statements.context: Post on the failures of peer review and the rise of pre-prints since COVID-19, with Elsevier profit margins as evidence of a broken academic publishing business. The author hedges that pre-prints may be a way around traditional publishing.
statements.note: Vague, phrased as a question with 'We shall see'; no concrete outcome.

statements.quote: These have been submitted to an excellent peer-reviewed journal, the American Journal of Therapeutics , edited by my friend and mentor Peter Manu, M.D. I look forward to their publication in the journal.
statements.context: Same post. The author's group has eight pre-prints on psychedelic medicine for primary care (introduction, LSD, DMT and ayahuasca, psilocybin, ibogaine, MDMA, ketamine, conclusion) submitted to the American Journal of Therapeutics; he expects them to be published there.
statements.note: Author's own work (control candidate); expectation that the submitted pre-prints will be published in the journal.
